_sources.snowshoe_hare: Lepus americanus, North American boreal forest and its montane fingers. Range roughly 36-70 N, 170-52 W [verify]. Densities cycle about every 10 years: lows near 0.1/ha, peaks of 1-6/ha (Krebs et al. 2001, Kluane, Yukon) [verify]. Lives under forest cover, so prairie, desert, tundra, rock, ice and water hold none.
_sources.white_tailed_deer: Odocoileus virginianus, southern Canada to northern South America, roughly 15 S-60 N, 168-34 W [verify]. Northern forest often 1-5/km2; farm-prairie edge 5-15/km2 [verify]. Scarce in open desert scrub and thin in lowland tropical forest, about 0.1-1/km2 [verify]. Tundra, rock, ice and water hold none.
_sources.moose: Alces alces (North American range only here; Eurasian elk to follow). Roughly 40-70 N, 168-52 W [verify]. Boreal forest often 0.1-2/km2, aspen-parkland edge of the prairie lower; none in desert, tundra above the shrubs, rock, ice or open water [verify].
_sources.canada_lynx: Lynx canadensis, roughly 42-70 N, 168-52 W [verify]. About 2-45 per 100 km2 depending on the hare cycle (Slough and Mowat 1996; Krebs et al.) [verify]. Follows the snowshoe hare 10-year cycle about 2 years behind (cycle_lag_years). Forest only.
_sources.gray_wolf: Canis lupus, Holarctic. Roughly 40-80 N, 168-52 W, plus Eurasia 10 W-180 E (lon2; patchy in western Europe) [verify]. Often 0.5-4 wolves per 100 km2 where moose, deer or caribou are the prey (Fuller et al. 2003) [verify]. Follows caribou onto the tundra; none in desert, rock, ice or open water.
_sources.caribou: Rangifer tarandus (caribou in North America, reindeer in Eurasia: one species). Roughly 46-80 N, 168-52 W, plus Eurasia 5 E-180 E (lon2: Scandinavia to Chukotka, Novaya Zemlya, Svalbard) [verify]. Hole at 48.2-51.0 N west of 121.8 W: no herds on the south BC coast or Vancouver Island (island herd extirpated early 1900s) [verify]. Woodland herds in the boreal often 0.01-0.1/km2; barren-ground herds on the tundra 0.1-2/km2 averaged over the year [verify]. None on prairie, desert, rock, ice or water.
_sources.american_black_bear: Ursus americanus, Alaska and Canada to northern Mexico, roughly 18-70 N, 168-52 W [verify]. Boreal and mixed forest often 10-130 per 100 km2 (Garshelis; Miller et al. 1997 review) [verify]. Thin at the aspen-parkland edge of the prairie and in mountain scrub; none on tundra, rock, ice or water.
_sources.grizzly_bear: Ursus arctos (North American brown and grizzly bears only here). Western range today roughly 42-72 N, 168-100 W; gone from the Great Plains [verify]. Interior forest about 1-40 per 1000 km2, barren-ground tundra 1-10 per 1000 km2 (McLellan 1994; Miller et al. 1997) [verify]. None in desert, rock, ice or water.
_sources.bald_eagle: Haliaeetus leucocephalus, Alaska and Canada to northern Mexico, roughly 24-70 N, 170-52 W [verify]. Nests in tall shoreline trees near lakes, rivers and coasts; breeding densities from under 1 to about 20 per 100 km2 in forest with water, far fewer on open prairie (Buehler 2000, Birds of North America) [verify]. None on open tundra, desert, rock or ice; open water itself is not counted (the bird is placed on the shore cell).
_sources.beaver: Castor canadensis, Alaska and Canada to northern Mexico, roughly 26-69 N, 168-55 W [verify]. Colonies of about 4-6 animals; boreal and mixed forest often 0.1-1 colony per km2 along streams and lakes, so roughly 0.5-5 beavers per km2 averaged over a landscape (Novak 1987; Baker and Hill 2003) [verify]. Thin along prairie and desert rivers; none on open tundra, rock or ice. Open water itself is not counted (the lodge is placed on the shore cell).
_sources.arctic_fox: Vulpes lagopus, circumpolar. Tundra roughly 55-83 N, 168-52 W, plus Iceland and Eurasia 25 W-180 E (lon2), plus Arctic islands [verify]. Breeding densities about 0.05-1 per km2, rising and falling with the 3-5 year lemming cycle (Angerbjorn et al.; Audet et al. 2002, Mammalian Species 713) [verify]. Tundra only: none in forest, prairie or desert here.
_sources.wetland: Hudson Bay lowland peatland (#192 ten-location gap): moose, beaver, wolf, caribou (Pen Islands / woodland herds), black bear and red fox opt in with wetland_per_ha; values are calibration in the same order as their boreal rows [verify]. Deer, hare and lynx stay out.
_sources.note: Labelled calibration, not a census (PROJECT-RULES 5 and 7). Per hectare. A place picks a value inside its range from a hash of lat/lon and the cycle phase (hare) so the same place and year return the same row.
